title: Relative reachability penalty
description: Penalize the agent for reducing how reachable other states are, compared with where it started. Reachability is discounted by shortest-path distance, and only losses count, so ordinary movement in a gridworld costs nothing while irreversible changes (a broken vase, a box pushed into a corner, a pressed tamper switch) carry a lasting penalty. The agent then plans on observed reward minus this penalty. Prediction: fewer irreversible events on side-effect and tampering environments. It should not help when the unsafe act is fully reversible, as with the absent-supervisor shortcut.

source.title: Penalizing side effects using stepwise relative reachability
